title: Fix boot1 false-positive RRAM write acknowledgment
description: Stock xous-core boot1 reports RRAM write_slice failures through DUART-only print_d! but unconditionally emits Wrote on the active USB/UART REPL for both legacy and CRC UF2 commands. Uploaders therefore cannot distinguish failed persistence from success. Track the upstream protocol correction without modifying the archived xous-core checkout here.
acceptance_criteria: Upstream boot1 emits an RRAM write failure on the active REPL transport and does not emit Wrote for that failed block. Regression tests cover both legacy and CRC UF2 commands, assert failed writes produce an in-band error, assert Wrote is suppressed on failure, and retain Wrote on successful writes. hal_bao uploader behavior is revalidated against the corrected protocol.

title: Add polling UDMA UART2 hardware console
description: Implement the smallest safe polling console for UDMA_UART_2 at 0x50103000 using the Xous REG_VALID/REG_DATA or descriptor-DMA behavior, with PB14 TX and PB13 RX already configured by boot1 at 1,000,000 baud 8N1. This is the first decisive on-hardware Zephyr execution marker; full interrupt-driven UDMA remains halbao-m4-udma.
acceptance_criteria: A devkey-signed Zephyr image prints a deterministic boot marker and hello_world output on Dabao PB14 at 1,000,000 baud; reset and repeated boots remain reliable; no interrupt-DMA scope is pulled forward.
notes:
Implementation delegated in zephyr-baochip using one-byte IFRAM TX descriptor, inherited PB13/PB14 pinmux, explicit UDMA clock/setup, and inherited RX-event cleanup.
Code review found boot1 handoff hazards not covered by clean builds: inherited continuous RX DMA may still target 0x5001f800, only RX event bit was sanitized although UART2 uses irqarray5 bits 8..11, and SETUP was changed live. Hardening is in progress to claim the full final IFRAM page, clear RX/TX DMA, sanitize all UART2 events, and derive divider from DT.

title: Add Baochip DUART simulation console
description: Add the baochip,duart binding and minimal TX-only polling driver for 0x40042000. Use TXD +0x00, CR +0x04, SR busy +0x08, ETUC +0x0c. Primary acceptance target is Verilator line output because Dabao does not connect PAD_DUART.
acceptance_criteria: Zephyr printk emits a deterministic boot marker in Baochip Verilator output; driver and binding build cleanly; documentation states that Dabao leaves PAD_DUART unconnected.
notes:
Implementation delegated in zephyr-baochip. DUART remains simulation-only for Dabao because PAD_DUART is unconnected.
Code review found poll_out needs serialization for concurrent thread/IRQ callers and ETUC/current-speed claims need alignment with proven RTL semantics. Hardening is in progress.
Validated exact hardened binary 87869730055ff7e94d55f2e27f64cd59fb47889d195b5e37f9d166522553fda4 in isolated Baochip Verilator. Captured `[duart] *** Booting Zephyr OS build 4.4.99 ***` and `[duart] Hello World! dabao/bao1x`; no trap, fatal, or panic. Evidence and verified logs are in .test-agent/m2-console-validation.

title: Standalone Rust boot1 UF2 serial sender
description: Build two focused Rust packages in hal_bao: reusable bao-boot1-protocol for canonical Baochip UF2 validation and boot1 REPL framing/negotiation/acknowledgment/retry behavior, plus executable-only bao-uf2send for serial-port discovery/transport and clap CLI. Implement USB CDC-ACM or physical UDMA UART transfer, has-crc probing, byte-wise echo disable plus settle, base64 block commands, exact acknowledgments, bounded retries, cleanup, and progress. Use upstream Python/source only as behavioral references; require no Python.
acceptance_criteria: bao-boot1-protocol exposes a typed, non-forgeable validated-image API and mockable transport with protocol tests. bao-uf2send is a thin documented CLI with explicit/list ports, baud/timeouts/retries, and serial adapter. Workspace fmt/test/clippy pass; real signed artifact passes preflight; hardware transfer remains required before closure.
notes:
Implement a standalone Rust equivalent informed by upstream uf2send.py and boot1 repl.rs behavior; do not invoke, embed, or require Python.
Implementation started: inspecting workspace conventions and Baochip UF2/REPL protocol references.
Implemented native Rust bao-uf2send crate and CLI: strict canonical baremetal UF2 preflight, port listing/explicit selection, configurable baud/timeout/retries, has-crc negotiation with legacy fallback, slow duplicate echo disable, base64+CRC commands, exact acknowledgments, bounded retries, and echo restoration. Mock boot1 tests cover CRC, legacy retry, mismatch, cleanup, family/address/slot rejection. cargo test --workspace and clippy -D warnings pass; the real 36-block signed Zephyr artifact passes host preflight. Remaining: no Baochip serial device is attached, so USB CDC/UART transfer timing, device acknowledgments, and post-write boot are not hardware-validated.
Architecture review recommended two packages: protocol library avoids pulling clap/serialport into consumers; executable package owns host serial UX. Also fix 100ms echo-disable settle, non-forgeable image API, typed errors, exact CRC test, and document boot1's misleading Wrote-after-write-error behavior.
Two-package refactor landed: bao-boot1-protocol contains opaque validated UF2 types, typed errors, mockable transport, configurable 100ms settle, exact CRC framing tests, negotiation/ack/retry behavior; bao-uf2send contains only serialport and clap host UX. Workspace fmt/test/clippy pass and the 36-block artifact preflights. Hardware transfer remains the only closure gap.
Protocol hardening commit 4e83cc74 adds typed DeviceWrite failure: a boot1  immediately aborts and cannot be superseded by its later misleading  line. CRC and legacy regression tests verify no retry and echo cleanup. ACK still cannot prove persistence against silent corruption or power loss.
Correction: protocol hardening commit 4e83cc74 adds typed DeviceWrite failure. A boot1 "Write error" line immediately aborts and cannot be superseded by its later misleading "Wrote" line. CRC and legacy regressions verify no retry and echo cleanup. ACK still cannot prove persistence against silent corruption or power loss.
Safety correction from stock xous-core 5d5bbbfa review: current legacy and CRC boot1 paths emit RRAM Write error only through DUART print_d!, then unconditionally emit Wrote on the active USB/UART REPL. Therefore ACK means command parsing only; bao-uf2send cannot detect stock boot1 persistence failures. SendError::DeviceWrite remains useful only for boot1 variants that emit an in-band error. Post-write boot1 audit of Next stage plus actual boot validation are required.
This safety correction supersedes the two earlier DeviceWrite notes: their fail-fast statement applies only when an error is present in-band, not to current stock boot1. No stock persistence-detection guarantee is claimed.

title: M2: ticktimer sys_clock driver
description: Implement the Zephyr sys_clock driver for the 64-bit ticktimer at 0xE001B000. The corrected RTL/Xous contract is in .design/research/07-ticktimer-sysclock.md: derive an exact 1 MHz post-divider TIME counter from the 350 MHz input with CLOCKS_PER_TICK=349 (reload-plus-one period 350), retain CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC=1000 and CYC_PER_TICK=1000, and express all timeout, elapsed, target, and last_count arithmetic only in post-divider counter cycles. Initialization disables the event, programs the divider, pulses CONTROL 1 then 0, waits until synchronized TIME zero is observed, establishes last_count=0, then commits a future first target before enabling direct IRQ 356. Read TIME high-low-high; commit targets high then low; treat the comparator as a level source and always disable/reprogram/W1C/enable. The ISR disables EV_ENABLE immediately, locks and advances last_count by whole tick quanta, and calls sys_clock_announce_locked with the event disabled; the kernel reprograms through sys_clock_set_timeout. Tickless mode programs requested absolute deadlines; periodic mode programs the next one-tick absolute boundary from sys_clock_set_timeout, not provisionally in the ISR. Planned integration covers driver, binding, DTS, Kconfig, CMake, and SoC clock configuration; timer0 is no longer the primary design.
acceptance_criteria: Dabao builds with tickless enabled and disabled without linking the RISC-V machine timer. DTS exposes ticktimer at 0xE001B000 size 0x24, 350 MHz input clock, and direct IRQ 356. Driver programs CLOCKS_PER_TICK=349 for an exact 1 MHz TIME counter, retains CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC=1000 with CYC_PER_TICK=1000, and never uses 350 MHz input-clock units in timeout, elapsed, target, or last_count formulas. Startup disables EV_ENABLE, programs the divider, writes CONTROL=1 then CONTROL=0, observes synchronized TIME=0 before trusting last_count=0, commits a future first target, clears stale pending, connects IRQ 356, and only then enables the event. Driver provides monotonic coherent k_cycle_get_32/64 and implements the locked sys_clock API. The ISR disables EV_ENABLE first, updates last_count under sys_clock_lock, calls sys_clock_announce_locked while disabled, and relies on the kernel post-announce sys_clock_set_timeout call to rearm. Tickless deadlines and periodic one-tick absolute rearm both catch up late service without drift. Verilator proves the 350-input-clock divider period, divider-before-reset synchronization, coherent rollover reads, high-then-low target commit, safe level-alarm ordering, direct dispatch, startup ordering, no provisional ISR enable, and both tickless and periodic behavior. Hardware demonstrates monotonic k_uptime, accurate k_sleep, bounded drift, tickless deadline wake, and periodic stability under load. Results must be recorded; implementation or validation is not implied by the research note.
notes:
2026-08-14: Ticktimer investigation is complete and implementation-ready in .design/research/07-ticktimer-sysclock.md. Proven details include nine-register map, reload-plus-one divider (349999 at 350 MHz for 1 kHz), coherent high-low-high TIME reads, high-then-low target commit, level comparator ordering, flattened direct IRQ 356, and inherited boot state. The note defines locked Zephyr state/API behavior, tickless and periodic algorithms, integration files, and build/Verilator/hardware gates. No Zephyr or Rust implementation and no validation are claimed.
2026-08-14 correction after design challenge: the original 1 kHz hardware-counter and preserve-inherited-TIME contract was wrong. RTL supports an exact 1 MHz counter with CLOCKS_PER_TICK=349 and reset loads the new divider into the prescaler. The corrected contract retains a 1 kHz Zephyr tick (CYC_PER_TICK=1000), requires CONTROL 1/0 followed by observing synchronized TIME zero before trusting last_count, keeps all accounting in post-divider cycles, and leaves EV_ENABLE disabled through sys_clock_announce_locked so kernel reprogramming owns both tickless and periodic rearm.

title: M2: early console — DUART simulation and UDMA UART2 hardware
description: Provide observable early Zephyr output on both validation targets. DUART at 0x40042000 is a TX-only debug block whose RTL emits completed lines, but Dabao leaves PAD_DUART unconnected; use it only for Verilator or another wired board. Dabao hardware output uses UDMA UART2 at 0x50103000 on PB14/PB13, 1,000,000 baud 8N1. TX requires an IFRAM DMA descriptor/buffer; REG_VALID/REG_DATA is polling RX only. Zephyr must safely take ownership from boot1 by quiescing inherited RX/TX DMA and UART2 events before enabling the console. Cross-check Xous bao1x-hal UDMA UART and DUART implementations.
acceptance_criteria: A Zephyr boot marker is visible in Verilator through DUART and on a Dabao PB14 serial capture through UDMA UART2. The board DTS chooses the hardware-visible UART console; no claim is made that DUART is connected on Dabao.
notes:
Correction from RTL and Dabao PCB: dedicated PAD_DUART exists in pad_frame_arm.sv but U1B DUART pad D3 is unconnected on dabao_v3c. PB13/PB14 belong to UDMA UART2. Earlier ticket wording conflated the two blocks.
Implementation delegated across the two child paths. UDMA TX requires a one-byte IFRAM descriptor at reserved 0x5001f000; REG_VALID/REG_DATA is RX-only. Drivers will mask inherited boot1 RX event state and preserve the no-system-clock bring-up configuration.

title: M2: irqarray interrupt controller driver
description: Implement Baochip ExternalInterruptArray: 20 LiteX irqarray banks plus direct ticktimer(20), susres(21), mailbox(22,23), and timer0(30) CPU lines. Use a flat Zephyr namespace with explicit event/direct mappings. Custom MIM 0xBC0 uses positive enable polarity; MIP 0xFC0 is read-only masked status and never EOI. EV_ENABLE is positive, EV_PENDING is W1C; edge children pre-ack and level children post-ack after source quiescence. Drain enabled pending while preserving shared-bank bits. Contract and race tests: .design/research/06-irq-ack-semantics.md.
acceptance_criteria: IRQs from at least two banks + ticktimer dispatch and ack correctly under load; nested/priority behavior sane.
notes:
R3 resolved in .design/research/06-irq-ack-semantics.md from primary RTL/Xous evidence. Implement positive MIM and EV_ENABLE masks; MIP is read-only masked status, never EOI. Edge events W1C before child dispatch and never post-clear; level events dispatch/quiesce peripheral then W1C. Trigger wins same-cycle W1C. Drain enabled pending, preserve shared-bank bits, and assert bank/direct-line mappings. Required Verilator races are listed in the note.
Driver/binding implementation delegated in zephyr-baochip using resolved research contract. Shared bao1x DTS integration is deferred until concurrent console DTS work lands.
Controller is now live in bao1x.dtsi and builds cleanly. arch_irq_* handles architectural IRQs 0..15, MMIO/MIM/MEIE transitions are ordered, ISR bounds include CONFIG_RISCV_RESERVED_IRQ_ISR_TABLES_OFFSET, Xous-confirmed rising-edge masks are encoded, and direct lines 20-23/30 are declared. Remaining acceptance: Verilator/hardware dispatch from two banks plus direct ticktimer and race/load validation.

title: M2: console + clock — DUART console, irqarray intc, ticktimer sys_clock
description: Make Baochip a functional Zephyr target. (1) Provide two distinct consoles: TX-only DUART at 0x40042000 for Verilator/boards that wire PAD_DUART, and polling UDMA UART2 at 0x50103000 on Dabao PB14/PB13 at 1,000,000 baud. (2) Implement 20 irqarray event banks plus direct CPU lines; MIM and EV_ENABLE use positive enable polarity, MIP is read-only masked status, and EV_PENDING is W1C with edge pre-ack/level post-ack semantics. (3) Implement ticktimer sys_clock at 0xE001B000 using direct IRQ line 20. See .design/research/00-soc-inventory.md and 06-irq-ack-semantics.md.
acceptance_criteria: Preemptive scheduling demonstrable: console prints, threads time-slice on ticktimer interrupts, IRQs from multiple banks dispatch correctly.

title: M1: soc/baochip/bao1x skeleton + 0x60060400 linker layout
description: SoC port skeleton in zephyr-baochip modeled on soc/litex/litex_vexriscv (4 files + soc.yml; no CLINT/PLIC needed — bao intc is MMIO + custom CSRs MIM/MIP 0xBC0/0xFC0). Files: soc.yml, Kconfig(.soc/.defconfig w/ CONFIG_BUILD_OUTPUT_UF2_FAMILY_ID=0xa7d76373), CMakeLists.txt, soc.h, custom linker fragment (ROM ORIGIN 0x60060400 LENGTH ~0x3F800, RAM ACRAM 0x61000000/2MiB, reset code FIRST linked byte for the JAL chain: sigblock jal +768, presign[0]=0x1000006f). Entry must reset mtvec/sp (boot1 leftovers), assumes M-mode/MMU-off/IRQs-masked/a0=KERNEL_START/a1=0. Details: .design/research/02-zephyr-integration.md §1, §7; .design/research/01-boot-delivery.md §3.
acceptance_criteria: Zephyr links for bao1x with __start exactly at 0x60060400 (verified via readelf/nm); initialized .data has a ROM LMA and the image fits the baremetal slot; SoC memory/ISA declarations pass Zephyr DTS/Kconfig build validation. Generated bao1x_peri.h remains the register-truth reference in hal_bao; subsystem drivers expose only their owned register subsets rather than importing the whole generated header into Zephyr.
notes:
Zephyr minimal and hello_world now link for dabao/bao1x. readelf: ELF32 RISC-V entry 0x60060400; nm: __start == __rom_region_start == 0x60060400, __rom_region_end 0x60062268. PT_LOAD for initialized .data has VMA 0x61000000 and LMA 0x6006225c. ROM use 7,784 bytes of 254 KiB. Remaining criterion is deciding whether to retain the generated-header shim requirement or use the more upstreamable DT/offset driver model.
Upstreamability decision: do not vendor/import the 1.2 MiB LiteX-environment header into Zephyr. Keep it and its SVD in hal_bao as provenance-backed register truth; implement small DT-first driver-local register subsets cross-checked against it and Xous.
close_reason: Baochip SoC metadata, Kconfig, startup sources, guarded linker layout, DTS memory/ISA declarations, and minimal board build are implemented. SDK builds verify __start/entry 0x60060400, .data ROM LMA, slot fit, and rv32imac_zicsr_zifencei selection.

title: M1: .data-capable image packer + devkey signer in hal_bao/tools
description: Plan-changing tooling item (risk R1). Stock xous-copy-object strips .data (poke table ≤40 words) — Zephyr needs a packer that embeds .data LMA in ROM and lets the kernel self-copy on start. Wrap/sign with xous-sign-image --bao1x --with-jump --sig-length 768 --function-code baremetal --loader-key devkey/dev.key (run inside xous-core for git-describe, or pass --git-describe). UF2: family 0xa7d76373, 256B payload/512B block, base 0x60060000. Spec: .design/research/01-boot-delivery.md §4-6.
acceptance_criteria: Packer consumes a Zephyr ELF, emits signed UF2 that boot1 accepts on the BAOCHIP volume; verified in verilator sim and on hardware.
notes:
Implementing host-side ELF-to-presign packer and signing wrapper first; hardware/simulator acceptance remains contingent on a linkable Baochip Zephyr ELF.
Implemented Rust bao-image crate. Reuses pinned xous-tools signer/UF2 and bao1x-api constants; ELF packer preserves PT_LOAD LMAs including initialized .data and enforces entry/slot constraints. Verified cargo test (5), clippy -D warnings, and real devkey signing: 1028-byte image -> 5-block UF2 with target 0x60060000/family 0xa7d76373. Hardware/verilator acceptance remains open until Baochip Zephyr ELF exists.
Ran end-to-end against the real Dabao Zephyr ELF: packed 7,784 ROM bytes (including .data LMA) into 8,040-byte presign image, signed to 8,808-byte Bao1xV1 baremetal image, and emitted 35-block UF2 with base 0x60060000 and family 0xa7d76373. Verilator/boot1/hardware acceptance remains.
Prepared manual hardware bundle at .test-agent/m1-hardware-validation with ELF, map, effective config/DTS, 8,196-byte presign image, 8,964-byte signed image, 36-block/18,432-byte UF2, and verified SHA256SUMS. Manual procedure: doc/bringup/manual-validation.md.
Canonical Xous signing/image-checker verified the hardware artifact: Baremetal, Ed25519ph developer key, anti-rollback 1, pq_enabled false, classical and overall verification PASSED. JSON report added to the local artifact bundle. Device audit is still required for revocation/PQ/local counter policy.

title: M0: scaffolding — vendor prefix, toolchain smoke test, regen path
description: Tree hygiene and toolchain validation before any SoC code. (1) Add 'baochip' to dts/bindings/vendor-prefixes.txt in zephyr-baochip + REUSE/spdx headers on new files. (2) Vendored bao1x_peri.h/.svd already in hal_bao/include (PROVENANCE.md records regen: rtl_to_svd.py --path ../../). (3) Toolchain smoke test: Zephyr SDK riscv64-zephyr-elf builds rv32imac_zicsr (gd32vf103 precedent, .design/research/02-zephyr-integration.md §5).
acceptance_criteria: A trivial riscv32 Zephyr build passes with the SDK toolchain; vendor prefix registered; every new file carries an SPDX tag.
notes:
Starting vendor-prefix registration and toolchain discovery. Zephyr SDK and west are not currently on PATH; structural work can proceed, but SDK acceptance needs installation or environment configuration.
Full Zephyr SDK 1.0.1 build now passes for board dabao/bao1x using samples/basic/minimal. DTS/Kconfig select rv32imac_zicsr_zifencei, XIP, 254 KiB ROM and 2 MiB RAM. This supersedes the earlier standalone compiler-only smoke test.
close_reason: Vendor prefix and SPDX hygiene are present, generated artifacts retain provenance, and a clean Zephyr samples/basic/minimal build passes for dabao/bao1x with Zephyr SDK 1.0.1 riscv64-zephyr-elf.

title: M1: boot to main — SoC skeleton, linker, .data-capable packer, signed UF2
description: The JAL-chain hump. (1) soc/baochip/bao1x in zephyr-baochip: soc.yml, Kconfig(.soc/.defconfig incl UF2 family id 0xa7d76373), CMakeLists, soc.h, custom linker — ROM ORIGIN 0x60060400 LENGTH ~0x3F800, RAM 0x61000000/2MiB; reset code must be the FIRST linked byte (sigblock jal +768, presign[0]=0x1000006f). (2) tools/ in hal_bao: custom image packer embedding .data LMA in ROM (stock xous-copy-object strips .data — ≤40-word poke table) + devkey signer (xous-sign-image --bao1x --with-jump --sig-length 768 --function-code baremetal --loader-key devkey/dev.key). (3) Handoff assumptions: M-mode, MMU off, IRQs masked, a0=KERNEL_START/a1=0, ~350MHz, DUART live, mtvec/sp must be reset (boot1 leftovers). Details: .design/research/01-boot-delivery.md.
acceptance_criteria: Signed UF2 image boots on Dabao (or verilator sim linked at RRAM base with --boot-offset 0) and reaches early shell/zephyr-entry; readelf confirms _start at 0x60060400 and .data present in ROM.

title: [epic] Zephyr RTOS port for Baochip 1x SoC and Dabao board
description: Port Zephyr RTOS to the Baochip 1x SoC (BAO1X2S4F-WA, VexRiscv RV32IMAC+Zkn, Sv32, no CLINT/PLIC) and the Dabao development board. Whole-SoC port, not a board port: the chip's only existing OS is Xous (Rust); there is no vendor C SDK. Zephyr code lands as new files in the zephyr-baochip fork; hal_bao holds vendored headers, image tooling, tickets, design docs. Reference implementation for all hardware behavior is xous-core. Full story: .design/init/init.md. Decisions/risks: .design/research/04-synthesis.md.
acceptance_criteria: hello_world boots on Dabao hardware via devkey-signed UF2 copied to the BAOCHIP MSC volume, with console on DUART (PB14/PB13 @1Mbaud), preemptive scheduling on ticktimer sys_clock, GPIO buttons readable, and the image toolchain (packer + signer + UF2) reproducible from hal_bao.

title: Integrate Baochip signed runner with Zephyr
description: Add a thin Baochip runner in zephyr-baochip only if west flash is desired. It accepts an explicitly produced signed UF2 path and delegates inspection/copy to bao-image. It must never select Zephyr's generic unsigned zephyr.uf2. Normal credential-free builds remain supported.
acceptance_criteria: Dabao can opt into a Baochip runner with an explicit signed artifact; generic unsigned UF2 is never selected; standard runner dry-run works; missing bao-image or signed artifact fails clearly.

title: Validate and safely copy signed Baochip UF2 images
description: Extend the Rust bao-image tool with canonical baremetal UF2 inspection and an optional explicit-target MSC copy. Validate magic, Baochip family, canonical 256-byte block profile, contiguous baremetal range, signed-header structure, and embedded-key signature where feasible. Clearly separate structural validity, embedded-key verification, and unknown device-local acceptance. Reject ALTCHIP and ambiguous targets; flush before success.
acceptance_criteria: Inspect reports canonical profile and signed-header metadata without writing and never predicts device acceptance. Optional copy requires an explicit or unambiguous BAOCHIP target, rejects ALTCHIP, supports normal opt-in dry-run, and flushes writes. Tests cover malformed profiles and target refusal paths.

title: M1: safe signed-image runner for Dabao
description: Provide a Baochip-specific signed-image generation and flash path before adding board.cmake. The generic Zephyr UF2 runner must not be used because zephyr.uf2 is unsigned and boot1 requires the 768-byte Bao1x signature block plus trampoline. The runner must consume bao-image output, validate every UF2 block, and make destructive developer-mode consequences explicit.
acceptance_criteria: Optional board.cmake integration selects only an explicitly configured signed Baochip UF2. A thin Baochip runner delegates format inspection/copy to bao-image, rejects ALTCHIP and ambiguous targets, supports Zephyr's normal opt-in dry-run, and never claims host inspection guarantees device acceptance. Manual MSC and upstream uf2send.py workflows remain supported.
notes: Reprioritized after primary-source review: manual MSC already works; Zephyr runners normally delegate to vendor tools and do not require custom confirmation UX. Generic uf2.py cannot discover boot1 because BAOCHIP has no INFO_UF2.TXT. Keep this small and P2; prioritize hardware-visible UDMA console.

title: Investigate: irqarray edge-vs-level ack semantics from Xous kernel
description: Risk R3 from 04-synthesis.md: irqarray ack semantics undocumented; wrong assumptions = lost or re-entrant IRQs. Trace the Xous kernel IRQ path (kernel/src) + per-peripheral drivers (uart, gpio, ticktimer) for the exact ack order (status-clear before/after handler, level vs pulse). Deliver an ack-contract note for the intc driver author.
acceptance_criteria: Ack-order contract documented with citations into xous-core; encoded as comments/assertions in the intc driver
notes:
Investigating irqarray/event semantics from baochip-1x RTL and Xous bao1x HAL; will document evidence and driver algorithm.
Resolved from baochip-1x RTL 83b220f and xous-core 5d5bbbf. Durable contract: .design/research/06-irq-ack-semantics.md. MIM/EV_ENABLE are positive enables; MIP is read-only masked status; irqarray pending is one-bit W1C with trigger priority. Edge pre-ack avoids loss; level post-ack follows peripheral quiescence. Implementation comments/assertions and race tests transferred to halbao-m2-intc.
close_reason: Primary RTL and Xous paths establish the complete ack/race contract in .design/research/06-irq-ack-semantics.md; downstream code assertions and Verilator tests are explicitly assigned to halbao-m2-intc.

title: Investigate: baremetal slot budget / RRAM layout growth path
description: Risk R2 + open question 1 from 04-synthesis.md: baremetal slot caps at ~254KiB before Xous kernel @0x6009FD00. Determine (a) whether boot1 slot config allows a larger baremetal region or relocation, (b) what a Zephyr image with console+intc+timer+gpio realistically sizes at, (c) whether XIP-only (.text in RRAM, .data in ACRAM) keeps us under budget. Sources: bao1x-boot slot config, baremetal/src/platform/bao1x/link.x.
acceptance_criteria: Written answer in .design/research/ with measured image sizes; go/no-go on slot renegotiation

title: M4: UDMA subsystem + interrupt-driven UART console
description: Descriptor-DMA subsystem shared by 4 UARTs + SPI/I2C/I2S: descriptor ring handling, channel arbitration, then UART2 interrupt console (the real console on PB14/PB13 — replaces DUART poll mode). Custom IP, reference = xous bao1x-hal UDMA drivers. Details: .design/research/00-soc-inventory.md §5.
acceptance_criteria: UART console in interrupt mode; SPI or I2C channel demonstrably talks to external hardware

title: M4: comms — UDMA subsystem, interrupt UART console, serial uploader
description: UDMA descriptor-DMA subsystem driver (custom IP; 4 UARTs + SPI/I2C/I2S channels behind it): shared descriptor handling first, then interrupt-driven UART2 console (the real console, PB14/PB13), then SPI/I2C as board needs demand. Optional: boot1 REPL 'uf2 <base64>' serial uploader (bio-loader pattern) for CI-less flashing. Details: .design/research/00-soc-inventory.md §5; .design/research/01-boot-delivery.md §7.
acceptance_criteria: UART console works in interrupt mode; at least one SPI or I2C peripheral talks to an external device; serial flasher documented.

title: M3: boards/baochip/dabao HWMv2 board definition
description: board.yml, devicetree (IOX gpio, duart console, ticktimer, wdt, rtc, buttons), Kconfig*, board.cmake referencing uf2 runner, image defs. Dissect one modern minimal riscv board under boards/ as template (.design/research/02-zephyr-integration.md §2, §7 skeleton).
acceptance_criteria: west build -b baochip/dabao/some-variant samples/hello_world succeeds end-to-end
notes:
Implementing the minimal upstream-shaped Dabao target early to unlock M0/M1 build validation. Initial DTS will contain only verified CPU, RRAM code window, and ACRAM; peripheral nodes remain deferred until bindings/drivers land.
Minimal upstream-shaped board target landed early in zephyr-baochip. Clean samples/basic/minimal and samples/hello_world builds pass for dabao/bao1x. Full ticket remains open for DUART/ticktimer/IOX/WDT/RTC nodes and safe signed-image flash integration.
close_reason: Upstream-shaped HWMv2 Dabao target, Baochip DTS, Kconfig, metadata, and documentation are present. Clean Zephyr SDK builds pass for samples/basic/minimal and samples/hello_world. Peripheral nodes will land with their owning M2/M3 driver tickets.

title: M3: IOX GPIO driver
description: IOX @0x5012F000: 6 ports PA-PF × 16 pins, 2-bit AFSEL, pull-up only, IRQs via INTCR/INTFR → PIOIRQ0-3. DT binding baochip,iox-gpio + Zephyr GPIO driver API. Reserved boot pins PC13 (PROG/USB-SE0), PB13/PB14 (console) must be documented/protected. Reference: utralib IOX block + xous gpio service.
acceptance_criteria: gpio_api/test suite passes (subset valid on-board); button input + header pad toggle verified

title: M3: board completeness — Dabao HWMv2 tree, GPIO, WDT, RTC
description: boards/baochip/dabao in zephyr-baochip: board.yml, DTS (IOX gpio@0x5012F000, duart, ticktimer, wdt, rtc, buttons RST_N/PC13), Kconfig, board.cmake w/ uf2 runner. Plus drivers: IOX GPIO (6 banks PA-PF × 16 pins, 2-bit AFSEL, pull-up only, INTCR/INTFR → PIOIRQ0-3), CMSDK WDT @0x40041000 (unlock 0x1ACCE551, feed 0x5A — standard IP, cheap win), PL031 RTC @0x40061000. NO LEDs on Dabao — blinky = UART print + button. Details: .design/research/00-soc-inventory.md §6-7; .design/research/02-zephyr-integration.md §2.
acceptance_criteria: west build -b baochip/dabao samples/hello_world produces flashable image; button sample reads PC13/RST; GPIO toggle observable on header pads; WDT feed keeps system alive.

title: M5: long tail — USB, BIO/SCE, Rust sample, Renode, upstreaming
description: Deferred work after the port is alive: USB CDC-ACM device driver (Corigine xHCI-style controller w/ USB3 caps — hard; bootloader stack not app-reusable), BIO coprocessor (4× PicoRV32 w/ FIFOs/IMEM/quantum) and SCE crypto (AES/SHA/PKE/TRNG/keyslots) as custom Zephyr subsystems, Rust app sample via zephyr-lang-rust module, Renode platform model (none exists today; verilator sim is the interim), Zkn exposure via riscv,isa-extensions, hal_bao split-out decision, and upstreaming to zephyrproject-rtos. Details: .design/research/03-rust-survey.md; .design/research/04-synthesis.md M5 + open questions.
acceptance_criteria: Picked off opportunistically; each gets its own ticket when activated

title: M3: CMSDK watchdog + PL031 RTC drivers
description: Two standard-IP cheap wins: WDT = ARM CMSDK @0x40041000 (unlock 0x1ACCE551, feed 0x5A; Xous runs ~30s period fed from ticktimer — wdt.rs:22-60,116); RTC = PL031 @0x4006100. Both have in-tree Zephyr analogues/bindings to adapt (CMSDK WDT driver exists for ARM boards; PL031 too). Details: .design/research/00-soc-inventory.md §3.
acceptance_criteria: wdt feed via sys_clock works; rtc readable, settable, alarm IRQ optional
